mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized growth > 2.5% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month indicates weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase does not correlate with weakening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the previous two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decrease does not correlate with weakening housing demand.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals strengthening supply-side conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with strengthening supply-side conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the previous three months signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with easing monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by less than 0.5% over the previous month, it signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with weakening consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the previous month signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint movement of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with strengthening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative over the previous quarter and housing starts (HOUST) decrease by more than 5% over the same period, it signals a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 0 and HOUST decreases > 5% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint movement of GDPC1 and HOUST does not correlate with broad-based demand contraction.
